architecture.title: Where Jev sits — code owns the workflow, Jev supplies typed judgments
architecture.caption: Your code builds state + typed questions and sends one HTTPS POST. Jev returns one typed answer per question (never prose). Deterministic policy in your code turns those answers into a proposal; actions stay behind separate authorization. In this course the key lives server-side in the repo-root .env and never reaches the browser.

sequence.caption: Measured live on jev-1.13.0: 478 input tokens, ~450-530 ms, $0.000020. The priority rule (P1 = event affected + explicit deadline) is ordinary Python you can read and test.

charts.title: What each Module 01 call cost
charts.caption: Measured live on jev-1.13.0 (2026-09-27). Three questions cost ~1.6× one question, not 3×, because the state is ingested once. At $0.042/Mtok the whole module is ≈ $0.0001.
